title: Background prebuild is cancelled by a draw that then defers the build itself
trigger: Boot with a populated pipeline cache so a pipeline key sits in deferred_graphics and the VkPipelinePrebuild pool is still running (background_active true). A draw for that key misses graphics_cache, so BuildNewGraphicsPipeline calls TakeBackgroundPipeline; the pipeline is not in background_ready yet, so the key is inserted into background_claimed and nullptr returned. If the 24 ms per-frame build budget is already spent (async shaders on, ShaderBuildBudget on), DeferRuntimeBuild returns true and the draw is skipped as 'build-deferred'. The worker then sees the key in background_claimed before starting (skips) or before publishing (discards its finished pipeline).
impact: No wrong image or crash. Wasted background CPU, and the pipeline is built again later on the GPU thread (or via async translation) when a draw next has budget; that is the hitching the prebuild was meant to avoid. Limited to the boot window while the background pool is busy.
reasoning: TakeBackgroundPipeline claims the key unconditionally while background_active, before DeferRuntimeBuild decides whether the GPU thread will actually build. The claim is only meaningful if the GPU thread builds, and the deferred path does not. Defaults make it reachable: use_asynchronous_shaders defaults true, Nx2Perf options are on unless switched off, BackgroundPipelinesEnabled is on unless EDEN_NX2_BACKGROUND_PIPELINES=0. Effect is performance only and only while the prebuild runs, and a later draw still gets a correct pipeline.
fix_note: Moving the claim after the DeferRuntimeBuild check is right: split TakeBackgroundPipeline into a lookup (take if ready) and a separate ClaimBackgroundKey(key) called just before the GPU thread actually builds or queues the translation. Side effect to watch: a key left unclaimed while deferred may be built by the worker and the GPU thread concurrently if a later draw proceeds past DeferRuntimeBuild after the worker passed its claim check; the claim at the build point plus the publish-time check already covers that, the result is at worst one duplicate build.

title: shader_infos[] can point at a ShaderInfo freed by cache invalidation
trigger: A graphics program is bound and cached (RefreshStages stored it in shader_infos[index]). The guest then overwrites that shader's code in place (e.g. reuses a shader pool slot); the write callback runs InvalidateRegion, which marks the entry and RemovePendingShaders erases the ShaderInfo from storage, bumping invalidation_serial but not Dirty::Shaders. The guest rebinds the program with the same offset/address registers, which Maxwell3D drops as a same-value write (SkipSameValueWrites default on) so Dirty::Shaders stays clear. The next draw changes only fixed-function state (e.g. blend), so the graphics key misses; RefreshStages returns last_shaders_valid early and GetGraphicsEnvironments dereferences shader_infos[index], which is freed memory. With a key hit instead, the old pipeline is reused for the rewritten code.
impact: Use after free read on the GPU thread (garbage lowered_native shared_ptr copy and size_bytes: crash or a corrupt/rejected shader build) in the key-miss case; stale pipeline (old shader output) in the key-hit case. Needs the guest to rewrite a live shader in place without changing any program register value, so rare. InvalidateRegion also runs on the calling CPU thread via ThreadManager::InvalidateRegion without GPU-thread synchronisation, which adds a data race on shader_infos[] readers.
reasoning: RefreshStages' early return skips all re-resolution while Dirty::Shaders is clear, and the only places that set it besides register writes are macro.cpp and RefreshDebugRejections (which comments exactly this hazard: 'shader_infos may point at removed programs'). RemovePendingShaders erases the unique_ptr<ShaderInfo> from storage and bumps invalidation_serial, but RefreshStages never compares it at the early out (it only reads it after the dirty check). GetGraphicsEnvironments then reads shader_infos[index] with no check for liveness. The window is real but needs an in-place rewrite plus no register change; the same structure exists in upstream yuzu so it seldom fires in practice.
fix_note: Either suggested fix works. Setting Dirty::Shaders on all channels from RemovePendingShaders (as RefreshDebugRejections does) is simplest but must be applied from the thread that owns the dirty flags, since InvalidateRegion can run on a CPU thread; safer is to record the invalidation_serial seen at the last refresh and compare it at the early out on the GPU thread. Cost: one atomic acquire load per draw, and a full re-resolve after any shader invalidation.
